With `ANOMALY_ACTION=throttle`, an app that triggered anomaly detection is paused for `ANOMALY_COOLDOWN_SEC`. This lifts the pause of one account × app at once. Recorded in the audit log as `anomaly.lift`.

The erasure is audited under the pseudonym only. Cannot be undone — call it when the account was deleted at its authorization server.

get.description: Consent requests and destructive-call confirmations, pending and decided, newest first.

Every tool, resource and prompt the gateway ships, including entries disabled for this deployment, with scopes, consent class, confirmation mode and annotations. Typed `studio_create_<type>` tools are generated per organization and are not listed.

Only for tokens the authorization server minted for its own backend (Studio / Web Client when they delete an account) — never for tokens of AI apps.

Only for tokens the authorization server minted for its own backend (claim `rb_first_party`, used by Studio and the Web Client when they delete an account); tokens of AI apps get 403.

info.title: roadbeat MCP Gateway — Admin & Integration API
info.description:
REST endpoints of the roadbeat MCP Gateway for administrators and the Studio Integration Hub: OAuth clients seen, activity and audit log, consent ledger, approvals, per-deployment catalog switches and GDPR export / erasure per principal, plus the admin UI bootstrap configuration and health probes.

Every admin and Integration Hub endpoint needs a gateway access token (audience = the gateway's `/mcp` resource) with the `mcp:admin` scope. The MCP endpoints themselves (`/mcp`, `/mcp/all`, `/mcp/{server}`) speak the Model Context Protocol, not REST — see "MCP endpoints" in this reference.

tags.name: integration-hub
tags.description: Catalog and consent API used by the Studio Integration Hub (`mcp:admin`).

tags.name: admin-ui
tags.description: Public bootstrap configuration of the admin UI at `/admin`.

tags.name: self-service
tags.description: The signed-in user’s own consents, and the account-deletion hook for the roadbeat services.

bearer.description: RFC 9068 access token (`typ: at+jwt`, asymmetrically signed) from a trusted authorization server, audience = `https://<gateway>/mcp`, scope `mcp:admin`.

clientId.description: OAuth client id (a Client ID Metadata Document URL or a pre-registered id).
Only revoke the consents given to this OAuth client.

confirm.description: Must repeat the principal id from the path — a guard against erasing the wrong account.

enabled.description: `false` hides the entry from every catalog view of this deployment.

ConsentClass.description: What a tool does with data. read_public and read_org need no consent; the other classes need a consent per (principal, OAuth client).

ConsentLifetime.description: once = for one successful call · day = 24 hours · days30 = 30 days · permanent = until revoked.

pseudonym.description: Random pseudonym the audit records were re-keyed to (`erased:<uuid>`); not derivable from the principal id.

audit.description: Audit records pseudonymized (incl. admin records naming the principal)

PrincipalExport.description: Everything the gateway stores about one principal, as one JSON document (sent as an attachment).

truncated.description: true when the audit history exceeded 50,000 records; the newest are included.

idempotency.description: Stored write results — metadata only, without the results themselves.

AdminUiConfig.description: Where the admin UI signs in. Public: it only names the authorization server and the UI's public client id.

configured.description: false when no authorization server for the admin UI is configured (the UI explains how to fix it).

clientId.description: The admin UI's public OAuth client id.

resource.description: RFC 8707 resource the admin token is requested for.

usesLeft.description: Remaining uses of a `once` consent; null otherwise.

ConfirmationRecord.description: A first-time consent request or a confirmation of a destructive call, decided on the approval page.

tool.description: Tool name, or `resource:<name>` for a resource read.

argsHash.description: SHA-256 of the call arguments (`consent:<class>` for consent requests). Arguments themselves are never stored.

summary.description: The human-readable text shown on the approval page.

ClientRecord.description: An OAuth client the gateway has seen (read-through mirror; the client registry itself lives at the authorization server).

issuer.description: Authorization server that issued the client's tokens (`local` for the stdio sidecar).

registration.description: `cimd` (client id is an HTTPS URL), `local`, or `unknown`.

id.description: Monotonic id; also the pagination cursor.

traceId.description: W3C trace id when the client sent `traceparent`.

name.description: Tool, resource URI, prompt or admin action name.

payload.description: Hashes and identifiers only (argsHash, destructive, resourceUris, idempotencyKey, confirmation mode, denial reason …) — never tokens or raw personal content.

nextCursor.description: Pass as `cursor` to get the next (older) page. Absent on the last page.

core.description: Part of the core catalog served at `/mcp`.

uri.description: Fixed URI or RFC 6570 URI template.

reason.description: Why the store is not reachable (only when not ready).

clientId.description: Only the consents given to this AI app (OAuth client id); omit for every app

Unauthorized.description: Missing, expired or untrusted token, or wrong audience
